message.content:
The sculpture most often cited as the quintessential masterpiece of the 19th‑century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin** (1889). ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Date** | 1889 – firmly within the 19th century | | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin, a leading figure of modern sculpture | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist, blending naturalism with expressive form | | **Impact** | • Became an icon of romantic love and human intimacy.
• Influenced countless artists and became a cultural touchstone.
• Its dramatic pose and emotional depth set a new standard for figurative sculpture. | | **Legacy** | • Widely reproduced in bronze, marble, and other media.
• Featured in museums worldwide (e.g., Musée Rodin, Paris; Musée d’Orsay).
• Continues to be referenced in literature, film, and popular culture. | While other 19th‑century works—such as Rodin’s *The Gates of Hell* (unfinished, 1880–1917) or *The Thinker* (1902–1904, technically early 20th) – are also celebrated, *The Kiss* is the most universally recognized and emblematic of the era’s artistic achievements.
